details: CONFIRMED. relay_rules.check() (lib/relay_rules.py:358) returns every stale target of projects.toml, the
checked project included (detect() names it after the main checkout's folder, the same key as
relay_rules.targets(), which doctor_parts already uses at the project part for "no stored spec rule").
The change cuts the list at machine_end, before `if root:`, so the whole rules line is machine-wide.
The probe output shows "proj" (the project being checked) inside the machine section.
The item's "What" is to stop OTHER projects deciding the exit code, not to stop the project's own rules from doing so.
Size: 15 agent minutes.
evidence: python3 -I scratchpad/probe_doctor.py (temp project set up as in the new test):
# This machine (does not change this project's exit code)
FIX  rules in sync  (global; demo; proj -> relay sync)
lib/relay_setup.py:1098-1101: stale = relay_rules.check(profile or {}); ok("rules in sync", not stale, ...)
failing_case: A project "proj" listed in projects.toml whose generated rules file differs from what relay sync would write.
`relay doctor <proj>` prints "FIX  rules in sync  (global; demo; proj -> relay sync)" under
"# This machine (does not change this project's exit code)"; if the project's other checks are ok it exits 0.
Before the change it exited 1. It should still exit 1: the project's own rules being stale is a fault of
this project (sessions there run on old rules). Only the OTHER projects' staleness (the item's
"alix; arsenal; ... noisegate" for tally) belongs to the machine part.
fix_hint: In the project part, add ok("rules for this project in sync", d["name"] not in stale names, "-> relay sync")
and keep the machine line for the other targets (exclude d["name"] from it when root is given).
pass_cases: 1. projects.toml has [proj] (the folder checked) and [other]; only proj's file is stale: doctor_parts(proj)
has a FIX for proj's rules in the project part; relay doctor proj exits 1 (other project checks ok).
2. Only [other]'s file is stale (the item's failing case, tally vs alix...): the project part has no rules FIX;
the machine part shows "rules in sync" FIX naming other; exit code follows the project part only (0 when fine).
3. Nothing stale: "rules in sync" ok, no rules FIX in either part.
4. relay doctor with no folder: one "rules in sync" line naming every stale target, counted in the exit code as before.
reason: tests/test_setup.py:98 (checked project's stale rules exit 1), :108 (another project's stale rules do not), :115 (nothing stale), :93 (no folder counts machine fix); 98, 108, 115 fail at base.
findings.summary: the checked project's own stale rules file is now a machine line, so relay doctor <project> exits 0 while that project's CLAUDE.local.md is out of date
